original_question: For which infinite structures S does the following Ramsey-type boundedness phenomenon hold: for every finite substructure A of S, there is a positive integer T such that whenever all copies of A inside S are colored with finitely many colors, one can find a subcopy S' of S in which the copies of A use at most T colors?
target_in_paper: Introduction, Question 1.3; in the paper's standing homogeneous-structure setting this is restated as Question 2.3(1). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core bounded-coloring phenomenon and the correct quantifier order of the paper's official formulation: fix a finite substructure A of S, ask for a bound T, and require that every finite coloring of copies of A in S admit a subcopy S' isomorphic to S on which at most T colors remain. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's ambient scope is not arbitrary infinite structures in full generality; unless otherwise specified, it studies countably infinite homogeneous relational structures. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
Section 2 fixes the setup in relational languages, beginning with a finite relational language whose relation symbols have finite arities. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))

The finite structures under discussion are those that embed into S, i.e. members of Age(S); your draft says only 'finite substructure' without tying this to the paper's Fraïssé/age language. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
A 'copy' of A in B is formalized via embeddings A→B and their images; the paper explicitly introduces copy notation for this. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
A 'subcopy S' of S' should be stated as an isomorphic substructure S'⊆S with S'≅S. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
The paper names the least such bound: if it exists, the least positive integer T is denoted T(A) and called the big Ramsey degree of A in S. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
In Section 2 terminology, the question is whether S has finite big Ramsey degrees, meaning that T(A) exists for every finite A embedding into S. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
refined_question: In the paper's default setting of countably infinite homogeneous relational structures S, for which such S does every finite structure A that embeds into S (equivalently, A∈Age(S)) have a finite big Ramsey degree T(A), meaning the least positive integer T(A) such that for every finite coloring of the set of copies of A in S, there exists a subcopy S'⊆S with S'≅S in which at most T(A) colors occur on copies of A? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for a countably infinite homogeneous structure K, does K have finite big Ramsey degrees; that is, does T(A) exist for every finite A that embeds into K? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official match because your draft is already essentially a paraphrase of Question 1.3 itself. The later Problem 6.1 is a narrower specialization to SAP Fraïssé classes, so it would broaden-or rather mis-target-your draft to replace Question 1.3 by that later problem. Section 2 supplies the hidden assumptions needed to make the question stand-alone and faithful to the paper: relational language, embeddings/copies, homogeneity, age, and the reformulation as existence of finite big Ramsey degrees. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))
